learning_outcomes.text: To offer the students with the basic principles, approaches, methods, technics that are used for managerial counting in the company.
To discuss key attributes of calculations linked with the budgeting, costing, project planning, financial sources and investment projects on prepared cases by lecturers and also by students.
To support teamwork ability on making cases and their presentation together with the basic communication abilities.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Economics for Technicians
Cost Control and Activity Based Management
Budgeting and Costing and used Methods- a brief overview
Cost Control in New Product Development Process - Target Costing
Project Management - basic terms, rules, project planning process
Project Management tools - project schedule and project budget
Introduction to Production and Operation management, Inventory Management
Introduction to Lean Manufacturing Concept
Business Planning
Financial Statements Analysis and Interpretation
Assessment of Sources of Finance
Capital Investment Appraisal
Final Conclusions and Recommendations.
Introduction to the Course, Rules and Requirements, Debate with the Students on their previous Experiences in this Area.
Economic Functions, their Optimal Points, Math and Graphical Solutions. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Operational Budget, its Structure, its Activities and Cost Counting. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Product costing, cost structures, cost calculation. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Target Costing - Simple Cases, Examples of the Utility and Technical Parameters and the Interaction with the Price of Product. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Project plan presentation. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Application of the CPM + PERT and other Basic Methods Linked with the Project Management. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Inventory Management Calculation - Basic Models. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Lean Techniques Application on Own Case. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Business Plan - Case Study. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Financial Statements Analysis - Examples. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Assessment of Sources of Finance - Examples. Introduction to the Next Seminar.
Capital Investment Appraisal - Case Study.
Final Test + Final Assessment.
bibliography: Freiberg, F., Zralý, M., Žilka, M.: Outlines, incl. solved cases in electronic form.
Atrill, P.: Financial Management for Non-Specialists, Prentice Hall, London 1997.
Rother, M., Shook, J.: Learning to See - Value Stream Mapping to Create Value and Eliminate Muda. Brookline, Massachusetts: The Lean Enterprise Institute. 2003.
